page.title: cc-smith storybook: every case
page.intro: Nine steps an Indian credit-card holder takes in cc-smith, each with its normal path, edge cases and failures. Every screen sits next to the calls made behind it, from the app to the backend, the rewards engine, the card-facts store, the ledger and SerpApi. Figures come from the backend's tests and one recorded user: HDFC Millennia on a shared HDFC limit and HSBC Live+ in its free first year, spending ₹59,000 a month.
page.rolloutLede: Hackathon submission first (10 Oct, 18:00 IST), then the three-month plan.

context.digest:
Product: cc-smith, for credit-card holders in India. Hackathon build for the SerpApi India Hackathon 2026 (Commerce & Market Intelligence), submission 10 Oct 2026 18:00 IST.

Facts: 22 cards in the catalogue, profiled from official bank pages (allow-list in docs/research/official-domains.yaml). A card fact is published only if (1) its URL is official for that field (bank for fees/earn/caps; co-brand partner for its reward currency; fintech operators like Kiwi and Scapia also for earn rules), (2) the verbatim quote is found in the fetched page or PDF, (3) every rupee amount, cap and percentage appears in its own quote, (4) range checks pass (earn ≤25%, fee ≤₹1 lakh). Otherwise it is speculation: shown as 'reported, not confirmed by the bank', never used in maths. No human review; every change alerts the owner. 21 merchant offers and 4 fee offers (LTF/FYF/joining waiver) from bank pages; one distributor copy is speculation. Money is integer paise. Fees include 18% GST.

A quick model (Haiku 4.5, 2.5 s limit, median 1.5 s measured) chooses the card at checkout from engine-computed figures and never calculates; rupee amounts in its reason must be supplied figures; timeout, error or invalid answer falls back to the engine's pick (decision D10). Checkout's engine pick is the best card for the month: this payment plus what the rest of the month still earns after it (spends prorated to the days left, under remaining caps and credit); ties go to the narrower rule, keeping broad caps like SBI Cashback's 5% on all online free. Engine: per purchase, rules matched by merchant > category > catch-all, then rule priority; exclusions; minimum amount; caps per period from the ledger; stacked bonus rules; UPI only for RuPay cards; memberships (Amazon Prime, Tata NeuPass, Kiwi Neon, paying bills through Google Pay) gate some rules. Finder simulates a year month by month, routing each spend to the best card, then hill-climbs whole-line moves so fee waivers and milestones are kept; adding a card can never score below the current stack minus its fee.

Decisions (owner): no affiliate money; no human in the loop (DR-12); hackathon first; Android only through M3; category spend amount is the total and merchants are part of it; per-card memberships; held cards can be LTF or FYF; shared credit pools; available credit = limit − (entered outstanding + logged payments − bills paid); notice board with reasons; payment capture manual until statement upload (M1) and notification/Gmail capture (M2); credit score is a user-entered band (no bureau API).

Open: premium tier undecided. Known gaps: report-wrong-info does not trigger a re-fetch although its response says so; score band not asked in onboarding; offer estimates take 'up to' figures at face value; fee-offer eligibility conditions are not checked against the user; Scapia Axis is treated as the Scapia Federal card; Airtel Axis 25%/10% rules not modelled; four cards listed but not scored (SimplyCLICK, Coral, AU LIT, Scapia). Live since 10 Oct: SerpApi key (22 searches used, 228 of 250 left) and Anthropic key; checkout model median 1.5 s with a 2.5 s limit; extraction runs live without strict mode; the first live Launch Radar sweep found 12 reported launches, with duplicates from headline wording.

s1.title: Tell it which cards you hold
s1.lede: An anonymous account, your cards, their limits and their fee status. Nothing else is needed to start.

s2.title: Say what you spend each month
s2.lede: A category amount is the total; merchants under it are part of it and are scored with their own rules.

s3.title: Ask which card to pay with
s3.lede: Checkout Advisor: every card you hold is checked for this one payment, in rupees. No language model runs on this path.

s4.title: See bank offers at the merchant
s4.lede: Live offers from the banks' own offer pages, shown next to the pick. They never change the ranking.

s5.title: Log a payment and watch available credit
s5.lede: Logged payments use caps and credit; a paid bill frees the shared limit.

s6.title: Find the next card
s6.lede: A year of your spends, simulated across your cards plus candidates, net of fees with GST, waivers and milestones.

s7.title: Read the notice board
s7.lede: The few things you must know now: why, what to do, rupees at stake, a date and the source.

s8.title: How a card fact gets in
s8.lede: No human review: a fact needs an official page, a verbatim quote, and every number written in that quote. Everything else is speculation.

s9.title: Watch new cards in the market
s9.lede: Google News and Google Ads Transparency (India) through one SerpApi gateway; a launch is scored only once the bank's own page confirms it.

g1.title: Payments are logged by hand
paras: Available credit, cap use and the cap notices are only as current as what the user logs. Most people will not log every payment.
Statement upload (M1) resets balances to the bank's figures each cycle; notification and Gmail capture (M2) log payments automatically. Until then, label available credit 'as of your last update'.

g2.title: Reporting wrong info doesn't re-fetch the page
paras: The report response says “the official page is re-fetched”, but no code triggers a fetch. The report only becomes speculation.
Either trigger a re-fetch of the card's official sources on report (cheap: the fetcher and pipeline exist) or change the message.

g3.title: Credit score is never asked
paras: The backend stores a score band, but onboarding doesn't ask for it, so approval likelihood isn't shown anywhere.
Add a score-band question with “don't know” to preferences (decision A3).

g4.title: 'Up to' offers counted at face value
paras: “Up to 25% … max ₹11,300” is estimated as the full 25%. That overstates the hint and the combined figure in the pay text.
Show “up to ₹X” for these and keep them out of the combined figure.

g5.title: Utilisation notice has no source
paras: The 30% guideline is general bureau practice, not a card term, so the notice has nothing to quote. Its wording says so, but nothing marks it as general guidance.

g6.title: Some cards earn less in the maths than in reality
paras: Airtel Axis's 25% Airtel and 10% utilities rules aren't modelled (their caps depend on the month's base cashback), and four cards (SimplyCLICK, Coral, AU LIT, Scapia) are listed but not scored because their base rate or point value isn't on an official page we could read.

g7.title: Fee-offer conditions aren't checked
paras: Swiggy ORNGE LTF (select corporates) and Magnus LTF (Burgundy Salary, ₹2 lakh a month) show to everyone. Asking employer type and salary band would let cc-smith hide offers the user can't get.

g8.title: Same launch listed several times
paras: The first live sweep listed IndusInd's corporate card and SBI's FD-backed card three times each, under different headline wordings (“Launches FD-Backed Credit Card”, “Advantage SBI Card”, “FD-backed YONO SBI Card”). An ad also produced a generic “SBI Credit Cards” candidate.
Group leads by issuer plus fuzzy-matched card name, and drop generic names before discovery. About 30 minutes with tests.

g9.title: Scapia Axis is treated as the Scapia Federal card
paras: Launch Radar marks “Scapia Axis Bank Credit Card” as already in the catalogue. Under DR-4's variant route it should be its own profile, since the issuer and terms differ.
